samples.question: This picture contains exactly one square panel with a solid dark border, plus a few much smaller dark specks scattered on the background that are decoration only. The panel's border encloses a seven-by-seven grid of forty-nine equal square cells; each cell is either dark (the same tone as the border) or pale (the same tone as the panel's background). Carry out this operation on that grid. Number the columns 0 to 6 from the panel's left border and the rows 0 to 6 from its top border. Slide the contents of each column upward, staying inside the panel and wrapping around from the top row back to the bottom row, by as many cells as that column's number: column 0 does not move, column 1 moves up by one cell, column 2 by two cells, and so on up to column 6, which moves up by six cells. Every cell keeps its own column; only its row changes. After all seven columns have been slid, the dark cells form exactly one of these four symbols. 'bars' is two fully dark horizontal rows, the second row from the top and the second row from the bottom, with every other cell pale. 'caret' is a fully dark bottom row together with one extra dark cell per column tracing an upward-pointing chevron: that cell is in the top row in the middle column, one row lower in each neighbouring column, and in the fourth row down in the two outermost columns. 'vee' is a fully dark top row together with one extra dark cell per column tracing a downward-pointing chevron: that cell is in the bottom row in the middle column, one row higher in each neighbouring column, and in the fourth row down in the two outermost columns. 'zigzag' is a fully dark middle row together with one extra dark cell per column, two rows above the middle row in the first, third, fifth and seventh columns and two rows below the middle row in the second, fourth and sixth columns. Whichever symbol is present, exactly fourteen of the forty-nine cells are dark and exactly two of the seven cells of every single column are dark; sliding the columns moves cells only within their own column and so changes neither of those counts. Neither the amount of dark ink, nor how it is spread across the columns, nor the panel's size, position or colour therefore reveals the symbol. As drawn, before the columns are slid, the dark cells match none of the four symbols. Which symbol do the dark cells form after the slide? Answer with exactly one of: bars, caret, vee, zigzag.
